observations: The badges are month-level counts and the search is a view filter, so the two are deliberately independent — narrowing the view must not make a manager think work disappeared.

c.recalc() runs off ng-change, one digest after the keystroke, so the row set has to be allowed to settle before it is read. Asserting on the next tick reads the pre-filter list and passes against the wrong data.
expected: Each status tab shows exactly the reportees whose timesheet holds that status for the displayed month.
"Not submitted" shows the reportees with no timesheet row at all.
Search narrows the visible rows to those whose name or employee id contains the needle, and does not move the tab badges, which are month-level.
actual: All five tabs agree with the timesheet records for July 2026.
Searching "Abel" narrowed 6 row(s) to 1, and the tab badges were unchanged.
case.verdictReason: Every tab and the search box filter the queue exactly as the records say they should.
